findings.summary: The maxClues cap is still evaluated from the per-tick snapshot for every card, so multiple harvest cards in one tick can still push the board past maxClues — the exact defect the rework claims to have fixed. harvestCard copies the snapshot into a local counter (`let boardClueCount = hd.boardClueCount`) and increments only that local; it never writes back to hd.boardClueCount, and runWrite never accumulates published clues into it either (the same `deps.harvest` object is passed to every harvest decision, and runChannelWrite sets boardClueCount once from assembled.clueEntities). With boardClueCount=63, maxClues=64 and two exited(0) cards each carrying one proposed_clue, card A publishes 1 clue (board=64) and card B recomputes headroom from the stale 63 and publishes another (board=65) — reachable even at the default --max-writes 5. Spec §1.6 requires that once the board has reached maxClues no new clue is added, and these writes are irreversible on an append-only bus with no DELETE. The in-code comment at src/harvest.ts:268-269 asserts the cap holds '单张卡（或多张卡累计）' and docs/dev-notes/dev_ledr_a8e_harvest_01.md:125-129 states the multi-card overshoot is fixed; neither is true. No test covers more than one harvest decision per runWrite call — test/harvest.test.ts:351-381 exercises a single card only.

The shipped deployment default reintroduces the `.board`→`.evidence`-style naming assumption that spec §1.4 forbids, just relocated from runtime code into the assembly script. EVIDENCE_CHANNEL defaults to `research:p02-smoke-1dce60.evidence`, i.e. the board channel TICK_CHANNEL (`research:p02-smoke-1dce60`, line 28) with `.evidence` appended. Spec §1.4's measured channel table states that `research:p02-smoke-1dce60` exists 「无任何后缀」 — no `.evidence` sibling — which is precisely why the spec bans deriving the evidence channel from the board channel name. Because publishing is append-only with no DELETE and this default renders into the fleet input consumed by the production `--run` path (fleet.yaml.tpl:8 → workflow.yaml:12 → tick.md:13), the first real V1 run would irreversibly publish evidence to a channel derived by string append rather than to a verified one. The code-level discipline (no default, loud failure) is correctly implemented; the defect is the concrete value chosen for the deployment default.

H15 requires a repository-wide grep proving no `.board`→`.evidence` derivation exists, but the test reads only src/harvest.ts and asserts a loose proxy (`not.toMatch(/replace\(/)`). It would not detect a derivation added in src/tick-run.ts, src/tick-entry.ts, or the shell/workflow assembly layer — which is where the derived default in finding 2 actually lives.
